players.product: memory (DRAM / NAND) and display-driver assembly & test

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue was NT$7,383 million, up 6.5% from Q1 and up 28.7% year over year, the highest quarterly revenue since 2014. Gross margin rose to 18.0% from 13.8% in Q1 (up 11.4 ppts year over year) on favorable product mix, pricing and utilization; operating profit was NT$948 million (12.8% margin) and net profit attributable to the company was NT$892 million, or NT$1.28 per basic common share (US$0.80 per basic ADS), a record since Q3 2022; return on equity was 14.4%. Chairman S.J. Cheng: demand continues to exceed capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue NT$7,383 million (+6.5% QoQ, +28.7% YoY); GM 18.0%; operating margin 12.8%; net profit NT$892 million; EPS NT$1.28

quarterly_data.signal: Overall utilization was 72% in Q2: assembly 78%, average test 74%, DDIC 69% and bumping 65%. Chairman S.J. Cheng: AI-driven demand continues to outpace available supply, customer visibility remains strong, and memory customers' restocking is expected to help improve assembly and test utilization.

Memory products were 51% of Q2 revenue, up approximately 6.7% from Q1 and more than 46% year over year. DRAM was about 20.7% of revenue, up about 1.3% from Q1 and more than 70% year over year; niche DRAM rose 21.8% from Q1. Flash was about 29.5% of revenue, up about 9.9% from Q1 and more than 32% year over year; NAND was about 34.6% of flash revenue (up 6.3% from Q1, up 15.9% year over year) and NOR flash rose 15.8% from Q1 and over 43% year over year. DRAM and SRAM together were over 21.5% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: memory 51% of revenue (+6.7% QoQ, >46% YoY); DRAM 20.7% (>70% YoY); flash 29.5% (+9.9% QoQ, >32% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: By service, assembly was just over 31.8% of Q2 revenue, mixed-signal and memory testing about 25.4% and wafer bumping about 23.7%; by product, DDIC was 18.1%, gold bumping about 21% and mixed-signal products just under 9.8%. By end market, automotive and industrial were just under 28.9% (up about 14.1% from Q1, over 45% year over year), smartphone about 29.9% (up about 2.8%), TV panel just over 12.6% (up 7.6%), consumer just over 22.2% (up about 12.2%) and computing 6.4% (down 23.7% from Q1).
quarterly_data.figure: assembly 31.8%; testing 25.4%; bumping 23.7%; auto & industrial 28.9%; smartphone 29.9%; computing 6.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Driver IC and gold bump revenue was about 39.2% of Q2 revenue, up about 7.1% from Q1 and about 14.1% year over year, helped by rush orders and a favorable mix of auto panel and OLED; DDIC revenue rose 9.7% and gold bump revenue about 4.9% from Q1 (over 29% year over year). Auto panels were more than 39% of DDIC revenue (up over 8.2% from Q1, about 23% year over year) and OLED just under 21.9% of DDIC revenue (up 12.7% from Q1) on customers' inventory replenishment.
quarterly_data.figure: DDIC + gold bump 39.2% of revenue (+7.1% QoQ, +14.1% YoY); DDIC +9.7% QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS selectively raised memory OSAT prices in Q2 to reflect material cost increases, and also raised DDIC OSAT prices. Chairman S.J. Cheng: material costs including substrates, lead frames and especially gold are rising and will be passed on to customers; high-end probe card prices for driver ICs have risen substantially and the company has reached agreements with customers to pass these costs through. He said customer conversations have been positive and the company does not intend to take advantage of customers.

Chairman S.J. Cheng: second-half 2026 performance is expected to remain strong on increased customer visibility, stable pricing and a favorable mix with DRAM leading and DDIC rush orders. Memory momentum is expected to be better than DDIC; DRAM is expected to see more significant growth in Q3 on strong DDR4 demand and the DDR5 ramp-up, while flash, affected by some customers' inventory adjustments, should stay steady on seasonal stocking but slightly trail DRAM. DDIC momentum is expected to improve further in the second half on seasonal OLED demand, automotive panels and rush orders.

Q2 capex was NT$2,380 million (12.1% bumping, 14.3% LCD driver, 30.5% assembly, 43.1% testing) and depreciation NT$1,218 million. The board approved an increased 2026 capex plan covering memory assembly and testing bottleneck stations, automation and AI, and testing capacity for silicon photonics and AI ASIC. CFO Silvia Su: 2026 capex will likely exceed 25% of revenue versus the usual target of about 20%, with logic and mixed-signal approximately 7%-10% of the full-year total; 2027 capex will likely exceed 25% of revenue again with a higher logic share. The expansion is funded partly by monetizing low-end, lower-utilization DDIC assets and an application for the government's Invest Taiwan subsidy.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capex NT$2,380 million; 2026 capex likely >25% of revenue; logic/mixed-signal 7%-10% of 2026 capex

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS recently acquired a new facility in the Tainan Science Park area to meet memory customers' capacity needs starting in 2027 and mixed-signal customers' expansion for new product projects; it is building memory testing capacity there to establish turnkey assembly and test, and consolidating clean room space for growth over the next three to five years.

Chairman S.J. Cheng: in logic and mixed-signal, ChipMOS plans to extend from TV SoC chips into mobile and AI ASIC-related testing; several mobile-related projects are ongoing, with new high-end testing equipment arriving at the end of this year for production, and further capacity to follow customer demand.

Chairman S.J. Cheng: ChipMOS is integrating its wafer bumping capacity, including copper pillar and gold bumping, with assembly technologies, giving it a strong position as it focuses on opportunities in the silicon photonics supply chain as a new long-term growth driver; the increased 2026 capex includes testing capacity for silicon photonics.

Cash and cash equivalents were NT$12,552 million at June 30, 2026, down NT$2,307 million from the start of the year; net free cash inflow for the first half was NT$736 million versus NT$1,667 million a year earlier, mainly on a NT$1,757 million increase in capex. Total assets were NT$46,964 million and equity NT$24,850 million; receivable turnover was 85 days and inventory turnover 70 days.
quarterly_data.figure: cash NT$12,552 million; H1 free cash inflow NT$736 million
